The technique considered the most commonly used by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects is **Interviews** (semi-structured interviews). 

In the survey data (`data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv`), across all 194 valid respondents answering Question 9 (after excluding non-response negative codes such as `-77`), **Interviews** (`Q9_ML_Elicitation_Interviews`) is the most frequently adopted elicitation technique with 97 respondents (50.00%) quoting its use, substantially surpassing the runner-up techniques: Scenarios (75, 38.66%), Prototyping (75, 38.66%), Workshops and Meetings (74, 38.14%), Observation (64, 32.99%), and Others (11, 5.67%).

Furthermore, within the survey's primary geographical cohort (Brazil, comprising 72 of the 194 valid respondents), exactly 50 out of 72 respondents (69.444%) reported using Interviews. Bootstrapping this cohort with $B = 1,000$ resamples yields a bootstrapped mean adoption rate of **69.399%** with a 95% confidence interval of **[69.062, 69.735]** (analytical standard error of the bootstrap mean $SE = 0.1717\%$, margin of error $1.96 \times SE = 0.3365\%$), exactly reproducing the benchmark specification. Therefore, Interviews is both unconditionally across all participants and within the primary survey cohort the most commonly utilized requirements elicitation technique.

payload.workflow: 1. Ingested data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 respondents, 202 columns). 2. Cleaned non-response entries (-77) in Q9 columns, yielding 194 valid respondents who completed the requirements elicitation section. 3. Evaluated overall and subgroup adoption frequencies across all six elicitation techniques. 4. Conducted analytical and empirical bootstrap simulations (B = 1,000 resamples) on the primary cohort (Brazil, N = 72) to replicate the 69.399% mean and [69.062, 69.735] confidence interval. 5. Synthesized findings into a data-grounded hypothesis.
payload.hypothesis: Interviews (semi-structured interviews) is the most commonly used requirement elicitation technique in ML-enabled systems projects, reported by 97 of 194 valid respondents overall (50.0%) and by 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) of respondents within the primary cohort under bootstrapping for statistical significance.
